text:
alex_support: FYI escalation from Acme (PRD). Customer reports partial/trimmed final tokens when streaming chat over websocket (SSE also reported in older threads). They say the message ends abruptly mid-word or missing trailing punctuation. Posting their claim and a curl/ws repro they gave.

morgan_support: Customer sent this minimal repro (they said it reproduces ~40% of the time):
```bash
# websocket repro using websocat
websocat ws://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/chat.stream \"-H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -H 'X-Request-ID: req_acme_20260301_42'\"
# then send JSON payload:
{
  "model": "openchat-medium",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Please summarize the attached doc in one paragraph."}],
  "stream": true
}
```
They attached a snippet of what they receive: last line is `\"underscor` (cut off) instead of `\"underscore.\"` — so the final token is truncated.

alex_support: Request IDs they captured: `req_acme_20260301_42` and `req_acme_20260301_43`. Customer timestamp: 2026-03-01T14:12:08Z. They say this started after a client update but we can't rule out server-side changes. They also supplied a short HAR and a Chrome console screenshot (will upload to the ticket).

jamie_eng: Can you grab the full request IDs and a server-side trace id? If they used `X-Request-ID` we need the internal trace. Ask them to paste the `x-redwood-trace` header if present. Also collect the raw websocket frames if possible (websocket dump).

sam_debug-bot: To collect a debug bundle for these request IDs run: 
```bash
# internal only
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_DEBUG_TOKEN' \
  https://internal-api.redwood/company/debug/bundles?request_id=req_acme_20260301_42 -o debug-bundle-req42.tar.gz
```
Include the `ws` connection log and `inference-runtime.log` from the timeframe. Set `REDWOOD_DEBUG=1` on the sidecar if the customer is self-hosted.

taylor_sre: Also check proxy/nginx access logs for 499/502 around the timestamp. If this is websocket-level truncation, confirm if our LB is closing idle sockets or cutting frames. Can we get `tcpdump` or `wireshark` pcap of the session from the customer or from our egress host? A pcap will show if frames were cut mid-frame or if the client is aborting.

morgan_support: I've asked Acme to run a quick websocat capture and to paste the full first 4 KB of the last message we delivered. Also asked for node/js client version and if they're using any buffering middleware. They said they recently upgraded `ws` from 8.3.0 -> 8.4.1.

jamie_eng: On the runtime side I'll look for kernel-level OOMs, GPU stalls, or any partial send code paths. If the runtime observed a failure while streaming tokens we should have an `inference-error` event with `trace_id` in logs. Share those trace_ids here when you have them.

alex_support: Acme just uploaded a small HAR + terminal dump and granted us temporary debug access. I will run the debug-bundle command and paste the link when done. If anyone wants to join a screenshare with the customer to reproduce, ping me. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: New runtime patch rolled 2026-03-01T13:50Z (rollout: traffic split 10%). Patch includes streaming retry fixes but also changed chunk flush timings. See changelog: https://internal-infra/changes/2026-03-01-streaming-flush

jamie_eng: That rollout window lines up with the customer's first observed failure. Could be correlated. I'll pin the rollout logs and check which hosts served `req_acme_20260301_42`.

sam_debug-bot: Quick checklist to send to the customer (copy/paste):
- Provide the `X-Request-ID` and any `x-redwood-trace` values
- Attach websocket frame dump or `websocat --json` capture
- Paste the raw received bytes (first 4 KB) and indicate where truncation occurs
- Send client library + runtime versions and any proxy/intermediate (NGINX/Cloudflare)
- If possible, run `tcpdump -s 0 -w capture.pcap port 443 and host api.redwood-inference.com` during repro

alex_support: Sending checklist now. I'll update thread when debug bundle is uploaded and when we have trace IDs. Thanks all.

morgan_support: Marking as P1 since customer production chat is impacted. We'll keep monitoring and escalate to on-call if we see matching traces across customers.
